stances_toward.note: Poland is the NATO and EU frontline that sheltered the exiled opposition (Tsikhanouskaya moved her office to Warsaw in Feb 2026), the jailed Polish-Belarusian journalist Poczobut was the main hostage, and the 2021 migrant crisis, the 2023 Wagner scare and the Sep 2025 closure of all crossings during Zapad-2025 define the rivalry; Russian drones entered Polish airspace partly from Belarus on 9-10 Sep 2025. Warming because of the 28 Apr 2026 prisoner swap (Poczobut for the archaeologist Butyagin, brokered with Washington), the 17 Nov 2025 reopening of Kuznica and Bobrowniki, and Sikorski's call for a 'new stage' - he also warned of a 'false dawn'. No source uses the word 'rival': our reading (confidence C). Bond - grievance: the Poczobut case, the Polish minority and 2021.

sources.title: Belarus eyes Western ties as it frees journalist Andrzej Poczobut

stances_toward.note: NATO, EU and V4 co-member; Babiš called Poland 'our closest partner' after the October 2025 election and met President Nawrocki in Prague on 25 Nov 2025, then posted with Tusk and Fico about waiting for the 'fourth musketeer'. Friction: Warsaw is the loudest Ukraine supporter in the region while the Czech cabinet has stopped paying, and the V4 had been paralysed by that split under Fiala. Stable because both want the V4 back in a form that excludes the Ukraine question. Bond - affinity: the Visegrad tie, shared eastern-flank worries.

stances_toward.note: The closest neighbour and the logistics hub of the war, aligned by necessity, with open friction: the Volhynia massacres (1943-45) and the May 2026 row over a Ukrainian army unit named after the UPA led President Nawrocki to strip Zelensky of the Order of the White Eagle; Zelensky skipped the Gdansk reconstruction conference on 25 Jun; 51.9% of Poles say the naming hurt their view of Ukraine. Prime Minister Tusk takes a conciliatory line and a Warsaw diplomat told Reuters that Ukraine's EU and NATO policy will still be set by the government. Exhumations resumed in 2025 (Puzniki). No bilateral treaty of alliance in this atlas, so 'reluctant ally', not 'ally'. Trend: cooling until August, with Nawrocki wishing victory but listing 'points of tension' on Independence Day. Bond - grievance: the historical wound.

relations_to.summary: Poland closed all crossings with Belarus on 12 Sep 2025 for Zapad-2025 and reopened Kuznica (passengers only) and Bobrowniki (EU-registered coaches and freight) on 17 Nov 2025; Kuznica had been shut since the 2021 migration crisis and Bobrowniki since 2023 over Poczobut.

sources.title: Poland reopens two border crossings with Belarus

relations_to.summary: Russian drones entered Polish airspace on 9-10 Sep 2025, some from Belarus (at least 19 drones, three downed); Poland invoked NATO Article 4; Belarus said the drones 'lost their course' after jamming.

sources.title: Russian drones breach NATO airspace in Poland, prompting alliance response

relations_to.summary: Prisoner swap on 28 Apr 2026: Belarus freed Andrzej Poczobut (1,860 days in detention) and Poland released the Russian archaeologist Butyagin, five detainees each way; Sikorski credited the Trump administration and warned of a possible 'false dawn'.

sources.title: Belarus eyes Western ties as it frees journalist Andrzej Poczobut
Poland and Belarus conduct prisoner swap including Polish journalist Poczobut

relations_to.summary: Tsikhanouskaya moved her main office from Vilnius to Warsaw in Jan-Feb 2026 after Lithuania downgraded her protection; the Vilnius office stays with its accreditation.

sources.title: Belarus opposition leader Tsikhanouskaya begins work in Warsaw after move from Vilnius

relations_to.summary: In May-June 2026 President Nawrocki stripped Zelensky of the Order of the White Eagle over Kyiv's naming of an army unit after the UPA; Zelensky skipped the Ukraine Reconstruction Conference in Gdansk on 25 Jun. Tusk called the quarrel a gift to Putin.

sources.title: Analysis: Poland and Ukraine's difficult history creates political minefield for Tusk
How to save relations with Poland and what Zelenskyy's visit to Gdansk has to do with it

relations_to.summary: Poland and Ukraine agreed in January 2025 to resume exhumations of Polish victims of the Volhynia massacres after Kyiv lifted its moratorium; work began at Puzniki, where at least 42 victims were found.
